title: Continuous-function condensation of topological modules
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative topological ring, and work on the coherent site of profinite sets in a fixed universe large enough for the coefficients [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. A topological $R$-module here is an $R$-module $M$ with continuous addition, negation and scalar multiplication $R\times M\to M$; morphisms are continuous $R$-linear maps. Use the sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. There is an additive functor $\mathscr C_R$ from these topological modules to internal $\underline R$-modules with the following specified formulas.

For every $M$, its underlying abelian sheaf is $S\mapsto C(S,M)$, with restrictions by precomposition and pointwise addition. Its action $\gamma_M:\underline R\otimes\mathscr C_R(M)\to\mathscr C_R(M)$ is the unique morphism whose restriction along the canonical map from the objectwise tensor presheaf sends $a\otimes h$ to $(s\mapsto a(s)h(s))$. This action satisfies the internal unit and associativity identities, so it is defined on the sheafified tensor, without an assertion that tensor-sheaf sections equal tensor products of sections.

For every continuous $R$-linear map $f:M\to N$, the underlying map of $\mathscr C_R(f)$ on $S$ is $h\mapsto f\circ h$; this is an internal $\underline R$-linear morphism. These maps preserve identities, composition and sums.

For every finite family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ with product topology, the canonical map
$$\mathscr C_R\left(\prod_{i\in I}M_i\right)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i\in I}\mathscr C_R(M_i)$$
is an internal module isomorphism, with section map $h\mapsto(\operatorname{pr}_i\circ h)_i$ and inverse $(h_i)_i\mapsto(s\mapsto(h_i(s))_i)$. For $M=R$ with its regular action, $\mathscr C_R(R)$ is the regular internal module over $\underline R$.

source.place: First two sentences: passing continuous linear coordinates and their inverse to internal condensed modules; expanded as a general continuous-function construction

proof.text: Put $B(S)=C(S,R)$, the ring sheaf of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and $P_M(S)=C(S,M)$ with precomposition restrictions. Addition and negation of sections are continuous by the hypotheses on $M$, and the abelian group identities hold at each $s\in S$. For a finite jointly surjective family $q_i:S_i\to S$ and compatible sections $h_i$, let $D=\coprod_i S_i$ and $q:D\to S$. The map $H:D\to M$ given by the $h_i$ is continuous. Compatibility on $S_i\times_S S_j$ says exactly that $H$ is constant on every fibre of $q$, so there is a unique function $h:S\to M$ with $hq=H$. The finite disjoint union $D$ is compact: restrict any open cover to each of its finitely many compact components and combine their finite subcovers. Since $S$ is Hausdorff, [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient] makes $q$ a quotient map. For an open $V\subset M$, $q^{-1}(h^{-1}V)=H^{-1}V$ is open, hence $h^{-1}V$ is open; thus $h$ is continuous. This proves existence and uniqueness of gluing on the finite covering families defining the coherent topology. On the empty profinite set there is one section, so the empty covering also satisfies the sheaf axiom. Therefore $P_M$ is an abelian sheaf. No separation hypothesis on $M$ was used.

source.place: First two sentences, underlying continuous-function sheaf; quotient-map descent expanded using the cited topology lemma

proof.text: Use the objectwise tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. For $a\in B(S)$ and $h\in P_M(S)$ set $(ah)(s)=a(s)h(s)$. This is continuous, being the composite of $s\mapsto(a(s),h(s))$ with the continuous scalar action. Pointwise distributivity gives $(a+a')h=ah+a'h$ and $a(h+h')=ah+ah'$. Consequently the assignment $a\otimes h\mapsto ah$ defines an abelian-group homomorphism $\beta_S:B(S)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}P_M(S)\to P_M(S)$: extend the formula additively on the generators and note that the two displayed identities respect the defining bilinearity relations of the tensor product. It commutes with restriction along $u:S'\to S$, because $(ah)\circ u=(a\circ u)(h\circ u)$. Hence $\beta:B\otimes_pP_M\to P_M$ is a presheaf morphism. With $\mu^p(a\otimes b)=ab$ and $e^p(n)=n\cdot1$, its presheaf module identities are $\beta(e^p(n)\otimes h)=nh$ and $\beta(ab\otimes h)=\beta(a\otimes\beta(b\otimes h))$. These follow respectively from $1h=h$ and $(a(s)b(s))h(s)=a(s)(b(s)h(s))$; additivity extends them from pure tensors to all tensors.

source.place: First two sentences, pointwise linearity before passage to condensed modules

proof.text: Let $a$ denote abelian sheafification and $\epsilon_P:aP\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ its canonical isomorphism for a sheaf $P$. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], $\beta$ extends uniquely to $\gamma_M=\epsilon_{P_M}\circ a(\beta):a(B\otimes_pP_M)\to P_M$. This is the required action on $B\otimes P_M$ of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], and its restriction is exactly $a\otimes h\mapsto(s\mapsto a(s)h(s))$. Apply the strong monoidal functor $a$ of that node to the two presheaf identities in step 2. Its structural isomorphisms identify $a(B\otimes_pP_M)$ with $aB\otimes aP_M$ and $a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$ with the sheaf unit, and its associativity and unit coherence identify the images of the presheaf associator and unitor with the sheaf ones. The isomorphism $\epsilon_B:aB\to B$ identifies the sheafified multiplication and unit with those of the given ring sheaf by [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf]. Conjugating the resulting identities by $\epsilon_B$ and $\epsilon_{P_M}$ gives precisely $\gamma_M\circ(\eta\otimes P_M)=\lambda_{P_M}$ and $\gamma_M\circ(\mu\otimes P_M)=\gamma_M\circ(B\otimes\gamma_M)\circ\alpha_{B,B,P_M}$. Thus $(P_M,\gamma_M)$ is an internal $B$-module by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. This argument uses sheafification and its monoidal comparison, rather than any formula identifying sections of a sheaf tensor with tensors of sections.

source.place: First two sentences, passage from pointwise scalar action to an internal condensed module

proof.text: For a continuous $R$-linear $f:M\to N$, define $P_f(S)(h)=f\circ h$. It is continuous as a composite, additive, and natural in $S$ since $f\circ(h\circ u)=(f\circ h)\circ u$. On pure tensors $P_f(ah)(s)=f(a(s)h(s))=a(s)f(h(s))$, so $P_f\beta_M=\beta_N(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes_pP_f)$ on all tensors by their defining additive generators. Sheafifying this equality, or equivalently using the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], yields $P_f\gamma_M=\gamma_N(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes P_f)$. This is exactly the morphism condition of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Evaluation gives $P_{\mathrm{id}}(h)=h$, $P_{gf}(h)=g\circ(f\circ h)$, and $P_{f+g}(h)(s)=f(h(s))+g(h(s))$. The sum $f+g$ is continuous by continuity of addition in $N$. Sums of the resulting sheaf maps are internal-linear: add the two action-commutation equations, using additivity of tensor on morphisms (objectwise and then sheafified) and of composition of abelian-group maps. These identities establish the functor and its additivity.

source.place: First two sentences, continuous linear coordinate maps and their inverses pass functorially to internal modules

proof.text: For a finite family put $M=\prod_iM_i$ with its product topology and coordinatewise operations. Those operations are continuous because each coordinate is the corresponding continuous operation on $M_i$. A map $h:S\to M$ is continuous exactly when all $\operatorname{pr}_ih$ are: preimages of the basic opens, which impose open conditions on finitely many coordinates, are finite intersections of open preimages. Thus $h\mapsto(\operatorname{pr}_ih)_i$ and $(h_i)_i\mapsto(s\mapsto(h_i(s))_i)$ are inverse additive bijections, commute with restriction, and respect the pointwise action of every $a:S\to R$. They therefore identify $P_M$ with the sectionwise product of the $P_{M_i}$ as abelian sheaves, with the action of step 3. This is also the internal-module product: for any internal module $K$ and module maps $v_i:K\to P_{M_i}$, the sectionwise tuple defines a unique natural additive map $v:K\to P_M$. Each projection of $v\gamma_K$ equals the same projection of $\gamma_M(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes v)$ by linearity of $v_i$ and of the projections; projections separate sections, so these two sheaf maps agree. Thus $v$ is a module map by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. This proves the product universal property and the stated isomorphism with its specified inverse. For $I=\varnothing$, the topological product is the zero module, $C(S,0)$ is a singleton for every $S$, and the same construction is the terminal internal module.

source.place: First two sentences, finite coordinate product of condensed modules and its inverse

proof.text: Finally take $M=R$ with its regular action. Then $P_R=B$ as abelian sheaves, including the restrictions. The presheaf action $\beta_R$ is $a\otimes b\mapsto(s\mapsto a(s)b(s))$, the objectwise multiplication of the ring sheaf. By [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf], the internal ring multiplication $\mu:B\otimes B\to B$ is its unique extension to the sheaf tensor. By the same uniqueness for $\gamma_R$ in step 3, $\gamma_R=\mu$. Hence $\mathscr C_R(R)$ is the regular internal module in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

split_report.summary: Constructed the continuous-function abelian sheaf by quotient descent, its tensor-presheaf action by bilinearity, and its internal action by strong monoidal sheafification. Checked functoriality and additivity, the explicit product comparison including the empty product, and the regular module. Reused existing DAG tools; no new nodes or statement changes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the first two sentences of lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md, specifically the passage of continuous linear coordinate maps and inverse maps to internal condensed modules and coordinate products.

tool_uses.why: Identifies sheafified pointwise multiplication and unit with those of the given ring sheaf; a generic ring-object normalization tool absent from this unit.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q22-ec9da0676 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and its six steps in full. There are no new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps, blueprint, import_flags and lean_audit are unchanged from side-live, where the item is unsplit and unreviewed; it is not on the dropped list and has no repair note. The source is lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md (main-20261015), whose first two sentences assert that the coordinate isomorphism C(-,F)≅C(-,E)^n is an isomorphism of E̲-modules; the item is the general construction behind that sentence, with proof_origin agent and no SGA. Step 1: compatible sections are constant on the fibres of D=⊔S_i→S; D is compact and S Hausdorff, so the cited Mathlib leaf (IsQuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous) applies and the glued function is continuous. The empty cover is checked and no separation on M is used. The step does not spell out the reduction from covering sieves to the generating finite families; that is the standard sheaf-for-a-coverage fact, accepted without a node. Step 2: the presheaf action uses the joint continuity of the scalar action that the statement assumes. Step 3: γ=ε∘a(β) is the unique extension; the strong monoidal sheafification of sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor and the counit normalization of det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf give exactly the unit and associativity identities of sk-def-sfb-module-objects. Step 4: linearity of f gives the morphism condition by sheafifying a presheaf equality; sums are pointwise, and id⊗(−) is additive. Step 5: a map into a product is continuous iff its coordinates are; the product universal property follows because the projections are module maps (step 4) and jointly monic; I=∅ gives the terminal module. Step 6: γ_R=μ because both are the unique extension of objectwise multiplication. Edge cases tested: zero ring, discrete R, non-Hausdorff M, M=R and E^n (what the citer lem-sfb-condensed-subfield-basis needs), empty profinite set, empty product. An rg -L search of the DAG for topological modules, C(S,M) and internal modules (def-pod-internal-module, lem-weil-pbc-integral-matrix-coefficient-transport, among others) found no duplicate. Accepted tool use: det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf, a generic ring-object normalization used as a black box. No changes.
